steps.text: I don't believe they would just go off the grid like this. House Nearl would not simply sit around.

a.text: I think so too. Their disappearance is quite curious.
You know as well as I do that the trail the hunter followed to the Golden Prairie went cold three years ago. No one's seen them since.
But even if we're all thinking this, you still have to take care of old Kirill, right?
...I've been thinking these past few years. A lot of people have their eyes on House Nearl.
They envy my brothers' honors, and despise a vagabond like me.

steps.text: But your older brother Schnitz is the greatest general of his generation. Why, with our own eyes, we saw him—
Who could deny his ability, even out of envy? Would they rather lose wars?

a.text: These people feel that wars are no longer necessary. Or rather, they don't want to face war anymore.
That's why they're sheathing their sharpest sword... and forcing me to return to the Grand Knight Territory.

steps.text: But you can't go back!
As I said, House Nearl can't simply sit around...

a.text: Why so excited, Czcibor? And why the frown?
Not sleeping well? Worried that the people we saved could be recaptured?

steps.text: No, I just...
I'm just thinking too much about this assassination.
...Assassination?
Oh, I'm dreaming.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: Do it.
December 1st, 2:15 A.M.
Outside Dzwonek

steps.name: Campaign Knight
steps.text: But...

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: Send word to the sentries inside. Do it.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: Everyone, get ready to move.

steps.name: Campaign Knight
steps.text: But our orders are to stay where we are.

steps.name: Campaign Knight
steps.text: Kawalerielki has everything under control.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: And?

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: Are those words enough to break a knight's spear? Have the bolts in your crossbows turned to dust?

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: The campaign knights are the only protectors that the panicking people will see. Can this fact be changed? Or does the Adeptus Sprawiedliwi Kazimierz lack the courage to muster even when Leithanien bares its fangs?

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: Our duty cannot be changed by a single word from the Adeptus Sprawiedliwi.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: Move. This is an order.

steps.name: Campaign Knight
steps.text: ...I'm sorry, sir, but you're no longer in a position to give orders.

steps.name: Campaign Knight
steps.text: The Adeptus Sprawiedliwi has revoked your command. The captains and the Craftsman's Guild have already been notified.

steps.name: Campaign Knight
steps.text: We fight for the glory of our knightclub, for the proper recognition of us campaign knights.

steps.name: Campaign Knight
steps.text: But the Grand Knight has the authority to veto all of it.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: ...So you won't obey?

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: Then I'll personally pass on my orders.

steps.name: Campaign Knight
steps.text: Ngh.. You...

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: The orders for Dzwonek have been issued. Everything shall proceed according to plan.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: All who assent, with me.
The captain sheathes his dark-red sword and marches past the camp tents.
Dozens of highly-ranked campaign knight are on duty, but they simply stand by the wayside.
No one joins him, or attempts to obstruct him. No one salutes.

steps.name: Staff
steps.text: I apologize, but due to a number of recent incidents, we are now required to inspect all vehicles that leave the city via the lift platform between midnight and 6 A.M. May I have your ID and documentation please?

steps.name: Bodyguard
steps.text: Here.

steps.name: Staff
steps.text: Thank you. A moment please.

steps.name: Staff
steps.text: And may I interest you in Dzwonek's specialty herb-flavored stockbeast jerky? It's quite a popular souvenir.

steps.name: Leithanian Noble
steps.text: No, thank you.
He waits impatiently, but the inspector's examination drags on.

steps.name: Leithanian Noble
steps.text: You see Leithanien's emblem, don't you? Is this really necessary?

steps.name: Leithanian Noble
steps.text: —Huh?

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: No need to worry about witnesses or public opinion at this hour.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: If the spire caster nullifies the bolts... you have permission to use javelins.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: No need to worry about the consequences either. None of the cities still remember how the campaign knights strike.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: Hey, old friend.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: You stand in my way once again.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: Should I feel relieved? That you're still willing to act, after all these years?

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: If you're here, then I suppose there will soon be an unexplained violent incident near Dzwonek, involving unknown parties.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: Bounty hunters and campaign knights... neither should ever come anywhere near a city that marches relentlessly forward.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: ...I only came to pick up my sword, as promised.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: You didn't come empty-handed, though.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: What about you? Your followers?

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: You know the answer to that.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: The Grand Knight Territory has intervened, as you hoped. The loyal knights acknowledge their new orders.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: For honor, for chivalrous order, for their long term interests... for the vain glory of their campaigns.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: The Grand Knight Territory has...?

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: Ah, it seems you didn't know.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: ...The Adeptus Sprawiedliwi Kazimierz casts its eyes along bloodlines. They know all that goes on in every corner of Kazimierz. This has nothing to do with me.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: My apologies, it couldn't have been you. You would not have begged for help from the Adeptus Sprawiedliwi and the Grand Knight.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: You came to convince me to turn back.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: But there is no way back, now that they've learned of the plan, and the Grand Knight has issued her orders.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: Besides, I've raised my sword against my own men, to give the order to begin the operation.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: Now that I know how hard it is to see a deed through to the end... it makes me admire what you did even more.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: ...Who do you think you are, to compare what you're doing to what I did?

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: I suppose I didn't provoke as many people as you.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: You're not provoking anyone... you're just contemptible.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: If you're not ashamed of your own actions, then why did you go to the convoluted lengths of leaking intelligence to pit me against the delegation from Leithanien?

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: No need to criticize my means. I'm simply as disappointed with you as I am with Kazimierz.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: Oh, right.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: The Adeptus Sprawiedliwi does not permit negative news about campaign knights to exist in writing. If I really did follow the order to stand down...

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: What do you think would happen to me? Would I die of a mysterious illness on my way back to the Grand Knight Territory, or be forever imprisoned beneath the tower, just like you?

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: You're in no position to talk about my life, Czcibor.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: If you insist on trying to decide for millions of people where the battlefield should lie, then you deserve your punishment.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: It is a campaign knight's duty to fight for the common folk.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: The unarmed are the first to be abandoned in war.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: ...You should have made a smarter choice.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: Even if it didn't involve returning to the campaign knights.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: 'I should have'? I should have ran from Kazimierz? Then why have you stayed, if you truly believe that leaving was the only correct choice?

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: Or should I have abandoned the plan in its entirety, even if this is my last chance?

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: You know better than I do that Kazimierz needs true violence. It needs a war that will turn it on its head.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: I've never once thought that way.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: Is that so?

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: All these years, we thought we knew each other so well. Well enough to leave certain things unsaid.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: Now I'm beginning to wonder just how much of that was all a misunderstanding.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: We should have sat down to talk, like the old days. Before a campfire in a forest clearing.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: ...If you weren't set on standing in my way right now, I'd have picked a branch and made a spear out of it, just like back then.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: You need to wake up.

steps.name: Bodyguard
steps.text: Stay down, sir! There are archers nearby!

steps.name: Leithanian Noble
steps.text: Who are they? First last night and now this, who could be after me?

steps.name: Leithanian Noble
steps.text: This is no checkpoint, Aloisia! We must go!

steps.name: Leithanian Noble
steps.text: Inspector, I suggest you get out of the way if you don't want to be run ov—
Now, now, don't be hasty.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Our guys have taken out the ones in your way. I suggest you relax and refrain from using Originium Arts.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: There are some traps here that are triggered by energy. And I doubt you'd enjoy the trip back to Leithanien if anything happened to your car.

steps.name: Leithanian Noble
steps.text: When did you—

steps.name: Leithanian Noble
steps.text: Nnnnnng—

steps.name: Bodyguard
steps.text: Sir!

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Oh, sorry.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: To put it simply, we would like this gentleman to come with us. May we have your cooperation?

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Serious advice. We're all screwed if the trap blows up.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: You're good, but not good enough to deal with everyone here. Can't hurt to hear me out, can it?

steps.name: Bodyguard
steps.text: There's nothing for us to discuss, mercenary.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Oh? Are you really thinking about setting it off, just to give your master a chance to escape?

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: That's why I never liked you spire casters. Nutjobs.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Chill out. This isn't worth any of our lives.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: The inspector isn't one of ours. Neither are the ambushing archers.

steps.name: Bodyguard
steps.text: ...Go on.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Ah, in the mood to listen now?

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Multiple groups fighting over the same objective is a fact of life in this line of work. Some people want to keep things safe, others want to watch it all burn.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Think about it carefully.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: There's a little village by the road to the southeast, about thirty minutes from here. On the highest building in the village is a shield emblem that looks like it could fall off at any moment.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: It'd make our jobs much easier if you waited there.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: ...Such a familiar light. The real Nearl.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: I've read the legend of Kirill, seen the Radiant Knight's name on banners in the streets, heard of your brother's blinding light from your own mouth.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: But this is only Nearl I know.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: It's just like in that banquet of betrayal... I thought I'd open the door to see the ground covered in blood, only to find myself bathing in a rain of light.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: ...That was many years ago.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: Indeed, being praised for old deeds is in itself a tragedy.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: What have you been doing all these years? Your sword is still sharp, your light even more disciplined.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: But there is enough power in your blade to parry even the weight of a heavy lance.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: Why do you ask when you already know the answer?

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: Because I don't believe you're powerless.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: I don't believe you couldn't have testified to Celina's innocence when she was being tried before the National Council. It would have taken a mere word.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: I don't believe that she could simply vanish without a trace without you so much as casting a glance at her.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: There are many things that I feel powerless about.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: I didn't think they could trap you.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: There was no point in testifying to her innocence. None of us could have saved her.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: The old you would never have said that. You would have pushed to have the justice you saw missing from the National Council codified into law.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: There were too many forces involved. Thirteen people were convicted. One law would not have brought them justice.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: So you measured their injustice against your life, and decided it was not worth the risk.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: Have you become afraid of death? Or have you simply decided that nothing is worth risking your life for anymore?
The campaign knight's blows fall hard.
His lance was intended to pierce armor and shields, creations of stone and steel.
But now, he aims his pent-up fury at an unseen foe.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: You're losing your balance, Czcibor. Don't make elementary mistakes.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: One more, and it'll be more than your armor that cracks.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: Ha...

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: We haven't sparred in ages, have we? Maybe I'm fiercer than you remember.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: And what about you? You never considered sheathing your sword when we tried to persuade you.
Another charge.
The lance smashes against the ground, sending gravel flying with Originium Arts sparks.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: Nice dodge.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: You didn't care what the disgraced nobles and blackmailed merchants thought. You didn't care about warnings from on high, or whether it was all for naught...

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: You would have exiled yourself from the Grand Knight Territory forever, gone out in a blaze of glory for justice.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: ...What about now?

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: If you can't do it, then stand aside and watch.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: I'll do what you should have.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: Who are you to judge what I should do?
Nearl's sword looks like it is simply shaking off the rain.
Scorching golden light falls upon the campaign knight's armor, leaving behind burn marks.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: You, who throws his life away callously, and refuses to turn back despite knowing that there is no hope?

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: ...I don't want you to die here.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: Your plan should not and will not succeed. What are you so obsessed with?

steps.name: Leithanian Noble
steps.text: *cough*, *cough* *cough*...

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Hey, you're awake.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Sorry, I was hired to cause you a bit of trouble.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: By the way, we're on a pharmaceutical delivery truck, and the windshield was broken by a stray bolt.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: It took quite a bit of effort to get you here. Fortunately, we can take a breather now that we're in the underground transport tunnels.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: This place is most chaotic in the early hours of morning. Outsourcing, irregular transactions, vehicles turned over 'accidentally'...

steps.name: Leithanian Noble
steps.text: Wh-What do you want? Where's Aloisia?

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Your bodyguard? She should be waiting outside the city, if she cooperates. I needed her to create a distraction.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Don't worry, no archer is going to be a problem for a caster of her skills.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: As for us... we're here to help, I guess, but we're not exactly doing this pro bono. And the client is a bit of a penny pincher, if you catch my drift.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: So, we've got a few wounded, and I think we ought to discuss your ransom. To cover the medical expenses, so to speak.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Now, will you be so kind as to put away your wand? I've always found casters from Leithanien to be a headache.

steps.name: Leithanian Noble
steps.text: ...Very well. I will pay a reasonable ransom, I will ask no questions, and I won't attempt to track you down afterwards.

steps.name: Leithanian Noble
steps.text: We shall negotiate like civilized people.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Excellent. I'm just doing my job. Once this truck gets the goods to the destination, it'll only be a short wait before we get out.

steps.name: Leithanian Noble
steps.text: ...I hear empty crates.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Oh, I'm not suggesting that you're the goods.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: The truck was rented, and the permit borrowed. Gotta put up appearances, after all.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Plus, in the event that something happens to your bodyguard, this cross-border business permit will give us a reason to drop you off outside Kazimierz.

steps.name: Leithanian Noble
steps.text: Who do you...

steps.name: Leithanian Noble
steps.text: Never mind, I don't want to know.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Good. Now how about we talk money, to pass the time?

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: You ask what I'm obsessed with?

a.text: This society has clear-cut rules. When the price of everything in life is clearly marked and labeled, it doesn't take a calculator to make the optimum decision.
But why are we not allowed to choose less wisely?
I know the Adeptus Sprawiedliwi Kazimierz invited you, as they invited every Nearl.
Not to mention the businessmen who would have every last knight humiliated in the arena.
You could have had great power, great prestige, great wealth. You could have saved so many people.
But you didn't.
You're a stubborn one too. Why are you trying to persuade me?

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: I returned to the ranks of the campaign knights, to the path of vassalage, in order to seek those who walk the same path.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: ...Do not misunderstand, Młynar. It's not war that I seek. War is inevitable, and the knights must carry that burden.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: Many have never seen the shadow beneath Leithanien's spire, never heard the wailing in the northern wind, which is why they can cheer for the blood spilled in the arena. But I bear no grudge against them.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: Chivalry may shine among the campaign knights, but it does not come from the glint of a sword. It is not authority through violence that I want to show people, nor the bones and smoldering ruins spread across the barrenlands.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: What I want to show them is that one does not have to trample upon other lives... That one can also choose to sacrifice oneself for others.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: That's what a knight sheds their blood for.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: The honor of a knight needs no testimony.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: How can you claim to uphold chivalry, when you have given up the ground on which you stand and left your fate to a war you have no control over?

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: Can you continue to shed tears and feel sorrow for the dead who line your path?
A drop of rain falls upon the tip of the spear.
The forest's night fog glows, as though the dawn has come early in the drizzle.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: Finally, you're not holding back your Originium Arts.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: I'm in full gear, while you're not even wearing basic armor. Is this really a fair duel?

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: What armor can bear the full brunt of a campaign knight's blow? Especially one from you?

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: Yes, it's perfect.

steps.name: Leithanian Noble
steps.text: Wait, you're...

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Hey, good eyes.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Some nobles didn't even realize until two months into our partnership.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Others realized it immediately, but kept their mouths shut as though they didn't know anything.

steps.name: Leithanian Noble
steps.text: Sarkaz mercenaries. Has the business machine of Kazimierz taken in your ilk too?

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: You flatter us. It's no skin off my nose whatever you think we are, but there are more than just Sarkaz hiding here.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Kazimierz treats us all equally... when it's deciding who to throw away.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Spooked?

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: The only thing unusual about a Sarkaz is that we live a bit longer than the average Kazimierzian. And I'm still pretty young.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: ...Although it's true that I have fewer and fewer old friends by the year.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: *cough*...
Silver shards litter the ground in the falling rain.
The broken armor cannot keep the blood inside.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: It's over.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: No...

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: Who do you want me to admit defeat to?
The campaign knight grabs his lance again and lunges forward.
But his legs do not move.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: ...Who do you want me to admit defeat to?
The knight stumbles and falls to his knees as the golden light rains down on his cheeks.
He raises his head and gazes at Nearl, his eyes wide open in the rain.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: To the nobles in the high tower of the Adeptus Sprawiedliwi Kazimierz, who spend their days in intrigue and vainglory?

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: Or to the merchants who cover up their dark deeds with false mirth, and disguise their twisted greed with contrived jest?

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: Do you want me to admit that I can never win against the tyranny of bloodlines?

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: Or do you want me to flee Kazimierz, abandon the struggle, and bow down to all that we despised?

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: *cough*...

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: I never saw another path worth taking.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: You still won't admit the only possibility, will you? Then prove it with your sword.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: If it's you who thinks I'm wrong, then... I'll accept it.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: I didn't lose to power, to money, to the will to survive, or to inexorable time.
Młynar sheathes his sword.
The rain of light continues to fall from the cold night sky before the dawn.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: Like I said... you don't need to die here.
If he turned back, it would stop, he thought.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: ...Hah.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: How do you live with it, Młynar?

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: Even though your fury burns so much fiercer than mine, even though you've seen the same things I have?

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: Don't tell me you don't see it...

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: The G.C.C. meddles with the campaign knights at will. More and more knights sell their honor and their swords to those merchants, fueling their increasing ambition.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: As for Leithanien... much time has passed since the fall of the Witch King's spire. I have seen with my own eyes their war preparations. There is no romanticism in it, only terror.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: And there will always be those who roam the barrenlands, made pariah by Catastrophe, war, and the evolution of the cities.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: You know all this, so... why do you not draw your sword?

a.text: His vision blurs and he cannot see Młynar's expression, only that he is still gazing down on him.
Why do you hesitate? What are you thinking?
He finds no answer in the rain, only golden starlight melting in his field of vision.
Every breath he takes is a struggle, as his life flows out along his cold armor.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: ...And that scornful sneer from up high, which awaits all who passionately pursue their ideals.

a.text: Not the numb spectators who snigger as I weep for the victims.
I feel equal sorrow from them as I do for the dead.
It's the ones who are even now sneering at my futile efforts against them.
Even if I banged my head so hard against this wall that my bones shattered into dust, there would be no echo.
The rain does not stop. His eyes remain wide.
He recalls the summer downpour, the muddy forest ground, the ring of wild flowers flowing on the stream.
He remembers the last good dream he had in those times.
You should not be so silent, Nearl, he thought.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: —Just like then, you must return to The Grand Knight Territory, after a long and futile journey.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: I don't believe you can let it go, Młynar.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: ...Their two names were erased just as they shined the brightest, like a fire thrown into a deep pool, going out without a trace.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: For fifteen years the Adeptus Sprawiedliwi has remained silent. Your questions have gone unanswered.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: House Nearl, bright as they are, was rejected by Kazimierz... The nation has sunken into darkness, and will not abide even a single ray of light.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: That's why you became disillusioned...

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: You... don't know how many years they've waited in foreign lands.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: ...What did you say?

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: Ha...

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: I encountered them a few years ago, when infiltrating Leithanien...
Drip.
A single drop of ink stained the last letter from home.
He never had the chance to send a letter asking the question that he harbored for twenty years.
After twenty years of silence, he knows this is the only thing he can ask the campaign knight.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: ...Did you tell anyone else about this?
Czcibor shakes his head.
Młynar waits in long silence for the next rebuke, and even longer for a word of repentance.
But the only response is a long exhalation, like a sigh, followed by the soft sound of clanging metal.
The campaign knight's body leans towards his lance that pierced the earth.
It is like one of the countless suits of empty armor they have seen on the barrenlands.
After a moment, Młynar kneels in the rain, making a gesture of mourning for his former comrade.
